quotes: A medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner must be requested in these rare circumstances.
claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately identifies the requirement to request a medical statement signed by a medical professional or health practitioner when eyeglasses cannot be removed for medical reasons.

The frames of the eyeglasses must not cover the eye(s);
claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately reflects the prohibition that frames must not cover the eye(s) when eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons.

quotes: If the eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons:
There must not be glare on eyeglasses that obscures the eye(s);
claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately conveys that glare obscuring the eye(s) is prohibited when eyeglasses are medically accepted.

quotes: If the eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons:

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately represents the prohibition against shadows or refraction from eyeglasses obscuring the eye(s).

unit_judgments.rationale: The overarching standard that 'Infants pose a particular challenge. The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained' was included in draft context quotes but was not formulated into a claim.
quotes: Infants pose a particular challenge. The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained:

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 fully covers the rule allowing an infant's/newborn's eyes to be partially or completely closed.
quotes: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0001 fully covers the permission to discreetly support an infant's head.
quotes: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0002 fully covers the acceptability of head tilt for infants.
quotes: Head tilt is acceptable for infants;

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0003 fully covers the prohibition of a parent's face appearing in the infant photograph.
quotes: A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0004 fully covers the adjudicator's duty to request a new photograph if submitted photos fail requirements.
quotes: You must request a new photograph if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements:

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0005 fully covers the requirement that photographs must be in color.
quotes: The photograph must be in color;

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0006 fully covers the recommendation/standard regarding timing (six months) and identification likeness.
quotes: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0007 fully covers the permission for changes in hairstyle or facial hair provided the photo remains a good likeness.
quotes: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant;

unit_judgments.rationale: The note regarding re-use of photographs from Certificates of Naturalization or Citizenship and USCIS processing times has no counterpart claim in the draft.
quotes: NOTE: Applicants may wish to re-use a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization. Be aware that even if the certificate itself was recently issued, because of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services processing times, the photograph may not have been taken within six months of submitting the application.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0008 fully covers the requirement that photographs must be free of material damage.
quotes: The photograph must be free of material damage:

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0009 fully covers the definition of material damage.
quotes: Material damage is any damage to the facial area that makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (e.g., creases, large holes, and large smudges) or impedes the functioning of facial recognition (damage in the area of the eyes);

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0010 fully covers the definition of immaterial damage.
quotes: Immaterial damage is any damage to the background, and non-material damage to the facial area (e.g., staple holes).

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0011 fully covers the acceptability of immaterial damage.
quotes: Immaterial damage is acceptable;

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0012 fully covers the exemption that the applicant does not need to sign the photograph.
quotes: The applicant does not need to sign the photograph, as this often causes creases or smudges;

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0013 fully covers the requirement for acceptance agents to sign the back of hand-carry application photographs.
quotes: For hand-carry applications, the acceptance agent signs the back of the photograph.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0014 fully covers the provision for returning an application to adjudication to request a new photograph if a printing defect is discovered.
quotes: Consequently, the passport application may be returned to adjudication to request a new photograph even though the photograph appeared acceptable.
